climate.overview_html: November opens with October 2026 confirmed as the projected warmest October in the ERA5 instrumental record — approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial October averages, extending the unbroken run above the 1.5°C Paris threshold to 13 consecutive months. The official Copernicus C3S monthly bulletin is expected later this week. COP31 opens in Antalya, Türkiye on November 9 — just eight days away; the presidency’s three action-agenda pledges (35×35 electrification, energy-efficient buildings compact, and AI climate pledge) are in place, and confirmed world-leader attendees for the November 11–12 summit include Brazil’s Lula and UK PM Burnham. Against this backdrop, UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed has called on nations not to use temperature overshoot as “a reason to surrender” climate ambition, as negotiators prepare to address NDC 3.0 ambition, the new collective quantified goal on climate finance agreed at COP29, and implementation of the Loss and Damage Fund.

items.headline: October 2026 Closes as Projected Warmest October in ERA5 History — ~1.76°C Above Preindustrial; 13th Consecutive Month Above 1.5°C Paris Threshold
items.summary: October 2026 closed yesterday as the projected warmest October in the ERA5 instrumental record, with global mean temperatures tracking approximately 1.76°C above preindustrial October averages, according to Copernicus C3S data cited by climate scientists Andrew Dessler and Zeke Hausfather. The figure represents a clear margin above October 2023, the previous record, and marks the 13th consecutive month with global temperatures above the 1.5°C Paris Agreement threshold. The exceptional warmth reflects compounding background greenhouse gas forcing and the record-strength 2026 El Niño. A celsius.earth ERA5-based model gives a slightly lower +0.23°C margin over October 2023. The official C3S monthly bulletin is expected in early November.

items.headline: UN “Overshoot Is Not a Reason to Surrender”: Deputy Secretary-General Urges Accelerated Mitigation, Adaptation and Loss-and-Damage Finance Ahead of COP31
items.summary: UN Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed called on world governments on October 30 not to use potential temperature overshoot of the 1.5°C Paris goal as a rationale for stepping back from climate commitments. Speaking nine days before the opening of COP31 in Antalya, she emphasised that the window to limit catastrophic warming remains open and called for accelerated action on emissions reductions, adaptation investments and operationalisation of the Loss and Damage Fund established at COP28.

items.headline: COP31: Brazil’s Lula Confirms World Leaders Summit Attendance for Nov 11–12; UK PM Burnham Also Attending; US Non-Participation Expected After January 2026 UNFCCC Withdrawal
items.summary: Brazil's President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva confirmed on October 30 that he will attend the World Leaders Summit at COP31 in Antalya on November 11–12. UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is also expected to attend. The US delegation status remains deeply uncertain following the Trump administration's January 2026 announcement of intent to withdraw from the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change. Brazil, as incoming host of COP32 in Belém in 2027, has a strong interest in the continuity of global climate negotiations.

items.headline: COP31 Presidency Announces Three Action-Agenda Initiatives: 35×35 Global Electrification Pledge, Antalya Compact on Energy Efficient Buildings, and Antalya AI Pledge
items.summary: The COP31 presidency hosted by Türkiye and co-facilitated by Australia announced three headline presidential initiatives ahead of the November 9–20 summit in Antalya. The 35×35 Global Electrification Pledge targets universal access to clean electricity by 2035; the Antalya Compact on Energy Efficient Buildings aims to accelerate building efficiency standards and retrofit programmes globally; and the Antalya AI Pledge commits signatories to using AI tools to drive emissions reductions and climate resilience. These are voluntary presidential action-agenda pledges that run alongside — rather than within — the formal UNFCCC negotiated text.

items.headline: COP31: Only 77 Heads of State Confirmed for Antalya — A Third Fewer Than COP28; Civic Space Concerns in Türkiye; Campaigners Demand Fossil-Lobby Access Limits
items.summary: With COP31 opening November 9 in Antalya, Climate Home News reports that only 77 heads of state or government had confirmed they would speak at the World Leaders Summit — roughly a third fewer than at the COP28 high-water mark in Dubai. The outlet highlights civil society concerns about civic space restrictions in Türkiye and calls from campaigners for limits on fossil-fuel industry lobbying. Brazil's Lula and UK PM Burnham subsequently confirmed attendance, incrementally raising the tally.

items.headline: Pacific Leaders Issue Taku Pakasoa Declaration Ahead of COP31: Commitments on Emissions, Climate Finance and Ocean Protection
items.summary: Pacific island leaders issued the Taku Pakasoa Declaration ahead of COP31 in Antalya, covering emissions reduction ambition, scaled-up climate finance for adaptation and loss-and-damage, and ocean protection provisions. The declaration represents a unified Pacific political position heading into the November 9–20 summit. Pacific nations have historically been among the most forceful voices for the 1.5°C temperature limit and for stronger finance commitments from developed countries.

major_events.name: Typhoon In-fa (JTWC 30W) — Track Reversal: Now Moving ENE Away from Philippines; Weakened to 155 km/h; No PAR Impact Expected
major_events.status: As of Nov 1 3 a.m.: PAGASA placed In-fa 2,290 km east of Extreme Northern Luzon with maximum sustained winds of 155 km/h and gusts to 190 km/h, tracking east-northeastward at 10 km/h — a decisive track reversal from October 31’s west-northwestward heading and a significant weakening from yesterday’s 185 km/h peak. The storm is now recurving away from the Philippines and over the open western Pacific. The earlier concern about PAR entry around November 5 is effectively resolved. PAGASA is still monitoring but has not indicated any direct impact on the country. Check JTWC and PAGASA for latest advisories.
major_events.impact: Philippines: No direct impact expected; track has reversed ENE. CNMI: Post-passage damage assessment for remote northern islands (Agrihan/Pagan/Alamagan) ongoing; main population centres Saipan/Tinian/Rota unaffected. Recurvature path may bring storm nearer Japan/Korea in the medium range — follow JTWC track.

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia/Borneo/Sumatra) — 120,000+ Satellite Hotspots; Indonesia–Singapore Joint Task Force Now Active; Schools Closed
major_events.status: As of Nov 1: Malay Mail reports hundreds of schools have been closed in Malaysia and Indonesia due to hazardous air quality; Indonesia has imposed a moratorium on new clearing permits for 66 million hectares of primary forest and peatland and created a new National Peatland and Mangrove Management Agency. The Indonesia–Singapore joint task force announced October 30 is now operational. More than 120,000 fire hotspot detections across Indonesia so far this season — approximately seven times the 2025 full-season total. Underground peat fires up to 8 m depth continue even as the wet-season transition begins.
major_events.impact: Indonesia: 333,470+ confirmed acute respiratory cases (7 provinces); ~1.9M ha burned; schools closing. Malaysia: schools closed in multiple states; Singapore: diplomatic task force active. ~40M people region-wide exposed to elevated PM2.5. CO₂ release expected to drive a measurable atmospheric CO₂ spike in November–December ERA5 data.

major_events.name: Cyclone Arnab Aftermath — Landfall Oct 28 Andhra Pradesh, India; 3+ Deaths; Strongest Post-Monsoon Bay of Bengal Cyclone Since 2014; Weakening Inland
major_events.status: As of Nov 1: Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Yanam on the Andhra Pradesh coast during the early morning of October 28, with maximum sustained winds of 125–135 km/h and gusts to 150 km/h, classified as a “very severe cyclonic storm” (IMD’s third-highest category) at landfall. It was the first named cyclone of the 2026 North Indian Ocean season and the strongest post-monsoon Bay of Bengal cyclone since 2014, killing at least three people and forcing thousands to evacuate in Andhra Pradesh districts. The system has since weakened significantly as it moves inland and is expected to dissipate. Flood and landslide risk remains elevated in interior Andhra Pradesh and adjacent Telangana through November 2.
major_events.impact: Andhra Pradesh, India: At least 3 deaths confirmed; thousands evacuated from coastal districts; crop and infrastructure damage ongoing assessment. Adjacent Telangana: elevated heavy-rain risk through Nov 2. Bay of Bengal sea-surface temperatures remain anomalously warm, supporting potential further cyclone formation during remainder of post-monsoon peak season.

weather.overview_html: The most significant weather development overnight is Typhoon In-fa’s decisive track reversal: PAGASA’s November 1 3 a.m. bulletin shows the storm at 2,290 km east of Extreme Northern Luzon, weakened to 155 km/h sustained winds and now moving east-northeastward at 10 km/h — away from the Philippines. The PAR entry threat from October 31 is resolved. Separately, Cyclone Arnab’s aftermath continues in Andhra Pradesh, India, following the October 28 landfall of the first cyclone of the 2026 North Indian Ocean season, the strongest post-monsoon Bay of Bengal storm since 2014. The Southeast Asian peatland haze continues with Indonesia–Singapore joint task force operations active and schools remaining closed across Malaysia and Indonesia.

items.headline: Typhoon In-fa Track Reversal: PAGASA Nov 1 Bulletin Shows Storm at 155 km/h Moving ENE — Away from Philippines; PAR Entry Threat Resolved
items.summary: PAGASA's November 1 3 a.m. bulletin placed Typhoon In-fa approximately 2,290 km east of Extreme Northern Luzon with maximum sustained winds of 155 km/h and gusts to 190 km/h — a significant weakening from October 31's 185 km/h and a decisive track reversal from westward to east-northeastward at 10 km/h. The storm is now moving away from the Philippines. The earlier PAGASA forecast of possible PAR entry around November 5 is effectively voided by this recurvature. A separate AllSaints' Day weather advisory for the Philippines noted enhanced rains in Luzon from the northeast monsoon and remnant moisture from In-fa's outer bands, with flash-flood warnings for several provinces. Check JTWC and PAGASA for the latest advisories.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab Landfall Oct 28 Near Yanam, Andhra Pradesh — 125–135 km/h Winds; 3+ Deaths; First 2026 NIO Cyclone and Strongest Post-Monsoon Bay of Bengal Storm Since 2014
items.summary: Cyclone Arnab crossed the Andhra Pradesh coast near Yanam during the early morning hours of October 28, making landfall as a 'very severe cyclonic storm' — IMD's third-highest category — with maximum sustained winds of 125–135 km/h and gusts to 150 km/h. ABC News and Down to Earth confirm at least three deaths and thousands of evacuations across coastal Andhra Pradesh districts. Arnab was the first named cyclone of the 2026 North Indian Ocean cyclone season and the strongest post-monsoon Bay of Bengal cyclone since 2014, reflecting anomalously warm sea-surface temperatures driven by the record 2026 El Niño. The system weakened rapidly after landfall and is expected to dissipate. Damage assessment continues across Godavari, Krishna and Guntur districts.

items.headline: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze: Indonesia–Singapore Joint Task Force Active; ~40M People Exposed; 120,000+ Hotspots; Schools Closed Across Malaysia and Indonesia
items.summary: The 2026 Southeast Asian peatland haze crisis enters November with the Indonesia–Singapore joint task force now operational following its October 30 activation. The Conversation and Malay Mail report more than 120,000 satellite fire hotspot detections across Indonesia this season — approximately seven times the 2025 full-season total — driven by the record El Niño-linked drought. Indonesia has imposed a moratorium on new permits to clear 66 million hectares of primary forest and peatland, and created a new National Peatland and Mangrove Management Agency. Underground peat fires at depths up to 8 metres are unresponsive to rainfall until the wet-season transition penetrates the full peat column. Approximately 40 million people region-wide are exposed to elevated PM2.5. More than 333,470 acute respiratory cases have been recorded across seven Indonesian provinces.

renewables.overview_html: The week’s largest new deal is Masdar’s October 28 memorandum of understanding with Invest New Zealand for up to NZ$1 billion (~US$585 million) in solar PV, wind and battery storage investment, linked to the New Zealand–UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement and open to co-investment with Māori businesses. In Europe, Nadara completed its purchase of the 48 MW Bettyhill Phase 2 onshore wind project in Sutherland, Scotland from Eden Renewables, targeting first generation late 2028, while IGNIS closed the sale of a 656 MWp portfolio of 28 development-stage Italian solar, hybrid and wind projects to flyRen Energy Group. These join the week’s earlier landmark transactions: Boralex’s Wind2 acquisition, Equitix’s Beatrice stake, and the 800 MW Great North Road Solar consent.

items.headline: Masdar Signs MoU with Invest New Zealand for Up to NZ$1 Billion (~US$585 M) in Solar PV, Wind and Battery Storage Investment
items.summary: UAE-based renewable developer Masdar signed a memorandum of understanding with New Zealand's investment promotion agency Invest New Zealand on October 28 to explore up to NZ$1 billion (approximately US$585 million) in solar PV, wind and battery storage investment in New Zealand. The MoU is linked to the New Zealand–UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement signed in 2024 and is open to co-investment with local and Māori businesses. New Zealand's Trade Minister Todd McClay described the arrangement as making the CEPA practical. New Zealand is targeting a doubling of its renewable electricity generation capacity by 2040. The arrangement is a memorandum, not a binding investment commitment.

items.headline: Nadara Completes Acquisition of 48 MW Bettyhill Phase 2 Onshore Wind Farm in Sutherland, Scotland from Eden Renewables; Construction Q1 2027, Operation Q4 2028
items.summary: Independent power producer Nadara completed its acquisition of the 48 MW Bettyhill Phase 2 onshore wind project in Sutherland in the Scottish Highlands from Eden Renewables. The site will comprise up to 10 wind turbines and was unanimously consented by Highland Council in February 2024. Construction is scheduled for Q1 2027 with commercial operations targeted for Q4 2028. Financial terms were not disclosed. Nadara operates a portfolio of wind and solar assets across Europe and the US.

items.headline: Boralex Acquires UK Onshore Wind Developer Wind2, Adding ~350 MW of Advanced-Stage Projects in Scotland, England and Wales; UK Pipeline Now ~2 GW
items.summary: Boralex announced the completion of its acquisition of Wind2, a UK onshore wind and renewable energy developer founded in 2016, on October 29. Wind2 brings approximately 350 MW of advanced-stage wind projects across Scotland, England and Wales. The deal lifts Boralex's UK development pipeline to approximately 2 GW, alongside 73 MW currently under construction. Financial terms were not disclosed. Boralex was taken private by La Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec in August 2026.

items.headline: Equitix Completes Acquisition of TRIG’s 17.5% Stake in 588 MW Beatrice Offshore Wind Farm for ~£155 Million; Equitix Now at 35% Ownership
items.summary: Equitix completed the acquisition of The Renewables Infrastructure Group's (TRIG) 17.5% stake in the 588 MW Beatrice Offshore Wind Farm in Scotland on October 29 for approximately £155 million, lifting its ownership to 35%. SSE Renewables holds 40% and Red Rock Renewables 25%; TRIG has fully exited the project. Beatrice, located off the Caithness coast and operating since 2019, is one of Scotland's largest offshore wind farms.

items.headline: UK Government Grants Development Consent for 800 MW Great North Road Solar Farm in Nottinghamshire — One of UK’s Largest-Ever Solar Approvals
items.summary: The UK government granted a Development Consent Order for the 800 MW Great North Road Solar Farm in Nottinghamshire on October 27, approved as a Nationally Significant Infrastructure Project under the Planning Act 2008. Developer Elements Green submitted the application in June 2025. The site covers approximately 1,765 hectares near Newark, with around 1,025 hectares allocated to solar arrays. The project was approved despite objections from local communities and farming groups over the loss of productive agricultural land.

items.headline: IGNIS Closes Sale of 656 MWp Italian Renewable Portfolio — 28 Solar, Hybrid and Wind Projects — to flyRen Energy Group; FlyRen Now Manages Over 2 GW in Italy
items.summary: Spanish developer IGNIS closed the sale of 656 MWp of renewable energy projects across Italy to flyRen Energy Group SpA, backed by Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II. The portfolio comprises 28 projects in various stages of development across multiple Italian regions, including photovoltaic, battery-hybrid and wind assets held through 23 Italian project companies. The transaction lifts flyRen's managed portfolio in Italy to over 2 GW. IGNIS described the deal as part of its ongoing asset rotation strategy to fund further Italian market growth. DWF and Green Horse Legal Advisory provided legal counsel; ValeCap acted as financial adviser to IGNIS.

items.headline: Iberdrola Prices $1.6 Billion Dual-Tranche US Green Bonds at 5.40% (3-Year) and 5.85% (7-Year) for US Transmission and Renewables; Book Demand Exceeded $2 Billion
items.summary: Iberdrola priced $1.6 billion in green bonds in the US market on October 27. The offering comprised two tranches: $800 million of 3-year notes at a 5.40% fixed coupon maturing November 2029, and $800 million of 7-year notes at 5.85% maturing November 2033. Proceeds will be applied to US electricity transmission infrastructure and renewable energy projects. Total book demand exceeded $2 billion. The deal closes November 4.

items.headline: EU Launches T-MED Investment Platform — Up to €4.5 Billion in EFSD+ Guarantees for Mediterranean Renewables, Green Hydrogen, Grids and Storage
items.summary: The European Commission launched the Trans-Mediterranean Investment Platform (T-MED) on October 26, providing up to €4.5 billion in EU guarantee capacity through EFSD+ to reduce investment risk and mobilise private capital for renewable electricity, green hydrogen, cross-border interconnectors, energy storage and clean technology manufacturing across the Mediterranean basin. T-MED sits within the broader Pact for the Mediterranean initiative targeting €25 billion in total investment by 2035.

items.headline: Optivolt Raises $32 Million Series A to Scale Module-Level Solar Power Electronics — VXI Capital Leads; 99.4% Conversion Efficiency Claimed
items.summary: Optivolt, a San Francisco startup developing module-integrated power electronics for solar panels, raised $32 million in a Series A round led by VXI Capital, with participation from RA Capital, Valo Ventures, Atlas Innovate and former SunPower CEO Tom Werner. The company's Power Balancer dynamically redistributes current among solar cell groups in real time, recovering output lost to shading and mismatch, claiming 99.4% conversion efficiency. Proceeds fund manufacturing expansion. Total funding: $42 million.

science.overview_html: Three new arXiv preprints in the last 72 hours mark an active period for atmospheric AI research: an agentic AI framework linking extreme-weather predictions to downstream agricultural-impact estimates emerged from NCAR (Oct 29); the FitzRoy model applied reinforcement-guided diffusion to precipitation forecasting over the continental US, targeting both skill and physical realism simultaneously (Oct 28); and HRRRCast demonstrated near-real-time data-driven regional forecasting verified against HRRR on extreme events (Oct 26). Earlier in October, Beucler and 11 co-authors published a major review arguing AI weather models must explicitly encode external forcings to respond credibly to greenhouse-gas perturbations — a prerequisite for bridging forecasting and climate projection. Ongoing context: Google DeepMind’s operational performance on Hurricane Isaias continued to attract scrutiny as the active 2026 season tests the limits of AI-only intensity forecasting.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.40641 — Agentic AI Framework Links Extreme-Weather Forecasts to Agricultural Consequences; NCAR / cs.AI × physics.ao-ph
items.summary: Researchers submitted arXiv:2610.40641 on October 29, presenting an agentic AI framework that connects extreme-weather event forecasts to downstream agricultural consequence estimates. The system couples a weather-event detection module with an agricultural impact model, enabling automated, end-to-end assessment from forecast output to expected crop, livestock or infrastructure effects. The work addresses a critical gap in operational weather services — translating high-impact weather warnings into sector-specific impact projections — and is cross-listed to cs.AI and physics.ao-ph.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.38775 — FitzRoy: Reinforcement-Guided Diffusion Model for Skillful and Physically Realistic Precipitation Forecasting over the Continental US
items.summary: The FitzRoy model, described in arXiv:2610.38775 (submitted October 28), applies reinforcement-guided diffusion to precipitation forecasting over the continental United States, jointly optimising for predictive skill and physical realism. Standard diffusion-based weather models tend to trade off one against the other — producing either sharp but physically implausible fields or smooth but oversmoothed outputs. FitzRoy uses a reinforcement learning reward signal to guide the diffusion process toward outputs that satisfy physical consistency metrics while retaining forecast skill. Results are evaluated against MRMS radar observations and standard probabilistic metrics.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.36186 — HRRRCast: Operational Data-Driven Regional Weather Forecasting with Verified Extreme-Event Skill and Near-Real-Time Capability
items.summary: HRRRCast, described in arXiv:2610.36186 (submitted October 26), is presented as the first data-driven regional weather model demonstrated to match the skill of NOAA's operational HRRR model on extreme weather events while operating in near-real-time. The 31-page, 22-figure paper validates the model against a set of verified high-impact events including severe convective outbreaks and extreme precipitation episodes. Near-real-time verification is a key step toward operational adoption of ML-based regional forecasting, addressing a major credibility gap compared with physics-based numerical models.

items.headline: China Introduces Two Operational AI Weather Models: Typhoon Cloud Pattern Recognition and 4-Hour Severe Convective Weather Prediction Using Fengyun Satellite Data
items.summary: China's Meteorological Administration unveiled two new operational AI weather models on October 30: one designed to interpret typhoon cloud imagery for storm structure and intensity analysis using Fengyun satellite data, and a second focused on predicting severe convective weather — including heavy precipitation and thunderstorm activity — up to four hours in advance. Both models are part of China's national initiative integrating deep learning into operational meteorological services.

items.headline: Google DeepMind AI Model Beat Physics-Based Forecasts on Hurricane Isaias Track — Florida Panhandle Landfall Correctly Forecast vs. Louisiana in Physics Models; Intensity Gap and Interpretability Concern Persist
items.summary: NPR's October 26 analysis reports that Google DeepMind's AI weather model outperformed traditional physics-based models on the track forecast for Hurricane Isaias, which made landfall near Destin, Florida as a Category 2 storm. The DeepMind model correctly indicated a Florida Panhandle landfall while physics-based models pointed to Louisiana. ECMWF's AIFS is described as the second AI model with strong track performance this season. However, AI trailed the NHC's blended consensus on intensity — a persistent gap — and researchers cannot explain why the model makes a given correct or incorrect forecast, a growing interpretability concern for operational use.

items.source: arXiv / University of Lausanne et al.
items.headline: arXiv:2610.09770 — Beucler et al.: AI Weather Models Must Encode External Forcings to Bridge Forecasting and Climate Projection; Major 12-Author Review
items.meta: Tom Beucler, David Neelin, Hui Su et al. (12 authors) · arXiv:2610.09770 (7 Oct 2026) · physics.ao-ph × cs.AI
items.summary: Tom Beucler and 11 co-authors (including David Neelin, Hui Su, Chris Bretherton, Laure Zanna and Tapio Schneider) submitted a major arXiv review on October 7, arguing that current AI weather models cannot credibly respond to greenhouse-gas forcings because they are trained only on historical reanalysis data without explicit representation of external forcings. The paper proposes a research framework that extends AI weather models to include forcing-dependent responses — a prerequisite for bridging weather prediction and climate projection. The authors stress-test the approach on out-of-distribution cases including extremes and counterfactual warming scenarios. Presented at IPAM UCLA and Cambridge's Newton Institute in early 2026, the preprint formalises a research agenda that has broad implications for the next generation of AI Earth system models.

items.headline: Nature Climate Change: South Indian Convergence Zone Rainfall Swings to Occur ~Twice as Often This Century — More Intense Rainfall per Event; Major Implications for Southern African Water Security
items.summary: A study in Nature Climate Change reports that climate model projections indicate swings of the South Indian convergence zone — a rainfall-producing circulation feature critical to Southern Africa — will occur approximately twice as often in the twenty-first century compared with the twentieth century, and will produce more intense rainfall per event. The dual signal of increased frequency and intensity has major implications for water security, flood risk and agricultural planning across Zimbabwe, Mozambique, South Africa and neighbouring countries.

items.title: Vaisala Completes Acquisition of AI Weather Company Atmo, Inc. — Announced June 2026; Deepens Vaisala’s Software and Services Strategy
items.body_html: Finnish weather-instrument and environmental-measurement leader Vaisala completed its acquisition of AI weather forecasting company Atmo, Inc. on October 29, roughly four months after announcing the deal in June 2026. Atmo builds machine-learning-based weather forecasting products and services. Vaisala said the deal “supports Vaisala’s strategic priority to grow its services and software revenue” and expand its AI and digital offerings alongside its traditional hardware and sensor businesses. Financial terms were not disclosed. The acquisition marks a significant consolidation in the weather-intelligence market, combining Vaisala’s global instrument network and data infrastructure with Atmo’s AI forecasting models.

items.title: Boralex Acquires UK Onshore Wind Developer Wind2 — ~350 MW Advanced-Stage Projects in Scotland, England and Wales
items.body_html: Canadian renewable producer Boralex completed the acquisition of UK onshore wind developer Wind2 on October 29, adding approximately 350 MW of advanced-stage wind projects across Scotland, England and Wales to its UK pipeline. The deal lifts Boralex’s UK development pipeline to approximately 2 GW alongside 73 MW currently under construction. Financial terms were not disclosed. Boralex was taken private by La Caisse de dépôt et placement du Québec in August 2026.

items.title: Equitix Completes £155 Million Beatrice Offshore Wind Stake Acquisition from TRIG — Now 35% Owner of 588 MW Scottish Project
items.body_html: Equitix completed the purchase of The Renewables Infrastructure Group’s (TRIG) 17.5% stake in the 588 MW Beatrice Offshore Wind Farm for approximately £155 million on October 29, lifting its holding to 35%. SSE Renewables (40%) and Red Rock Renewables (25%) hold the remaining ownership; TRIG has fully exited the Scottish project. The transaction, first announced in July 2026, completed on schedule. Beatrice is located off the Caithness coast and has been operating since 2019.

items.title: IGNIS Closes 656 MWp Italian Renewable Portfolio Sale to flyRen Energy Group — 28 Projects; flyRen Now Manages Over 2 GW in Italy
items.body_html: Spanish developer IGNIS closed the sale of a portfolio of 656 MWp across 28 renewable-energy projects in Italy to flyRen Energy Group SpA, which is majority-owned by Foresight Energy Infrastructure Partners II. The portfolio covers PV, battery-hybrid and wind projects across multiple Italian regions, held through 23 special-purpose vehicles. With the transaction, flyRen’s managed portfolio in Italy surpasses 2 GW. DWF and Green Horse Legal Advisory provided legal counsel; ValeCap acted as financial adviser to IGNIS.

items.title: Optivolt Raises $32 Million Series A to Scale Smart Solar Panel Power Electronics
items.body_html: Optivolt, a San Francisco startup developing module-level power electronics for solar panels, closed a $32 million Series A led by VXI Capital, with participation from RA Capital, Valo Ventures, Atlas Innovate and former SunPower CEO Tom Werner. The company’s Power Balancer dynamically redistributes current among solar cell groups in real time, claiming 99.4% conversion efficiency. Total funding: $42 million.

items.title: CESC/Purvah Green Extends ReNew 1.4 GWp Acquisition Deadline to November 21 — Original Oct 31 Deadline Missed; ∼$510 M Deal Still Pending
items.body_html: India’s CESC Limited and its renewable arm Purvah Green Power have amended the share purchase agreement for their ~1.4 GWp ReNew Solar Power acquisition, extending the closing deadline by 21 days to November 21, 2026, after the original October 31 deadline lapsed without completion. The deal, announced in August 2026, covers six special-purpose vehicles holding approximately 1.4 GWp of contracted, operating solar capacity at an enterprise value of approximately  4,859 crore (~US$510 million). More than 90% of the acquired capacity is contracted with the Solar Energy Corporation of India. No regulatory approvals were originally required; the reason for the deadline extension was not disclosed.
